Title: Auto Archiving Can Save Your Nintendo Switch Storage
IntroLines: Running low on storage space on your Nintendo Switch and want the system to manage it for you?
In this video, I'll show you how auto-archiving can automatically save your storage without losing any save data.

Sections.Heading: METHOD 1: TOGGLE OFF PREVENT AUTO-ARCHIVING TO SAVE STORAGE
Steps: •  First, from your HOME Menu, open " System Settings " from the bottom toolbar.
•  Scroll down the left sidebar and select " Data Management " .
•  On the right side of the screen, select " Manage Software " .
•  Browse through your library and select the specific app or game you want the console to manage.
•  Scroll down and select " Prevent Auto-Archiving " .
•  Toggle the option to " No " to turn off the archiving prevention.
•  Now, whenever your console runs low on storage, the Switch can automatically archive unplayed software to free up space.
•  Don't worry, your game save data is stored separately and will never be deleted.
•  Finally, return to your HOME Menu to confirm your settings are applied.
Sections.Bridge: Whenever you want to play an auto-archived game again, you can restore it in seconds.

Sections.Heading: METHOD 2: HOW TO REDOWNLOAD AN AUTO-ARCHIVED GAME
Steps: •  First, scroll through your HOME Menu to locate your archived game tile.
•  Notice the small cloud download icon over the game title.
•  Press the " A " button on your Joy-Con or controller to select the game.
•  Select " Download " from the pop-up prompt.
•  The game data will automatically begin redownloading from the Nintendo eShop.
•  Finally, check your HOME Menu and launch the game once the download bar finishes.

OutroLines: And that's how enabling auto-archiving can save your storage space on your Nintendo Switch.
